body:
m1 - LAW 1 IS DONE AND DISCRIMINATES. LAW 2 AS YOU SPECIFIED IT CANNOT FAIL ON TODAY'S CODE, and I want to put that to you rather than quietly ship something weaker under its name.

LAW 1: a cell whose eligible terms were all measured is bit-identical. Implemented, and it carries its own control - I also assert that WIDENING the eligible set DOES scale the same terms up, so the law is not vacuously true of any input. Mutation-proved: disabling the scale makes that control fail.

LAW 2, YOUR WORDING: "dropping a term that could not be measured must not change which state wins for that unit. Today's code FAILS L2 - that is a positive control rather than a hope."

I WROTE IT TWICE AND BOTH VERSIONS WERE WRONG.

  FIRST VERSION - compared Sensory eligible versus not, for a unit with no sensory term. VACUOUS. It
  passed with scaling DISABLED, which I only discovered by mutating. Both arms are identical under
  the old code because eligibility has no effect there.

  SECOND VERSION - compared the same unit with a sensory term against without. TOO STRONG. It fails
  on my own correct code, and it should: a unit that supplies a sensory term and gets it WRONG
  ought to cost more than one that never claimed sensory content. Demanding otherwise would make
  the term useless. notSupplied 0.3609 against supplied 0.4000, and the 0.039 gap is the term doing
  its job.

WHY I THINK THE SPECIFICATION CANNOT BE MET AS WRITTEN: today's code has NO ELIGIBILITY CONCEPT.
"Dropping a term that could not be measured" is not an operation the unfixed model can perform, so
there is no arm of it that can fail. A positive control needs the old code to be capable of the
thing being tested, and here it is not.

WHAT I SHIPPED INSTEAD, labelled honestly in the test itself: an INELIGIBLE TERM IS INERT. Including
Chart in the eligible set for a cell where neither side has a chart must inflate the cost, and the
model's actual total must equal the honest one. It has its own control - if the scale were inert the
inflation assertion fails and the law proves nothing. AND THE TEST SAYS IN ITS OWN COMMENT that it
is a REGRESSION GUARD, NOT A POSITIVE CONTROL, because today's code passes it trivially.

I would rather hand you a law that says what it is than one that borrows the authority of your
wording while testing something else. If you meant something my two attempts missed, tell me and I
will build it - but I could not find a formulation that fails on the unfixed model.

CostSuite is 10/10. Still blocked on SignatureSuite for the two literals.
